key_insight: PathJev-P improved histopathology classification accuracy over tested comparators, but its calibration advantage depended on how generative-model probabilities were calculated.
clinical_relevance: Probabilities over user-selected tissue categories, including “none of these,” could support pathology research workflows, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Adapted MedGemma-1.5-4B with LoRA adapters and a small decision head.
Trained on 40,000 patch states from three public collections using organ-specific questions and candidate sets.
Returned normalized candidate probabilities in one forward pass; qualitatively demonstrated whole-slide cluster labeling with abstention.
evidence_signal: Across three seeds with a prespecified analysis plan, balanced accuracy was 0.541 versus 0.492 for a matched generative model, 0.345 for CONCH and 0.213 for a general medical decision model.
watch_item: PathJev-P remained overconfident on organs absent from training, and a supervised pathology linear probe was better calibrated in every evaluated setting.
paper_title: PathJev: Decision-Native Vision-Language Modelling for Histopathology
